$comment: Mid-century Modernism motion data: limited animation in the manner of UPA cartoons and Saul Bass title sequences. Poses change on twos (12 drawings a second, a new pose every 83 ms) or threes (8 a second, every 125 ms) and then hold. In CSS, stepped timing is steps(n, end) over a duration of n x 83 ms or n x 125 ms. Timings are rules of thumb derived from 24 fps film practice, not measured from specific films.
character: Hold, then snap. Things sit still long enough to be read as a poster, then jump to the next pose in a few stepped drawings. Shapes cut on, slide in as bars, or morph into the next idea. Nothing drifts and nothing floats.

onTwos.use: Default for character and shape moves.

onThrees.use: Slower, more graphic moves: morphs, title bars, background changes.

onOnes.use: Only for very fast actions (a snap, a flick) of 2-4 frames.

springs.$comment: Springs are used only to compute pose targets (where an overshoot lands); the result is then sampled on twos or threes, never played smoothly. stiffness k, damping c, mass m.

snap.use: Arrive with no overshoot in 3-4 stepped drawings. Bars, panels, type blocks.

pop.use: One overshoot drawing (about 12%) then settle: the emblem appearing.

squash.use: Character beats: a bird hopping, a cat landing. Two overshoot drawings.

twos.use: A 500 ms move drawn on twos (6 drawings). Scale the step count with duration / 83 ms.

threes.use: A 750 ms move drawn on threes (6 drawings). Scale the step count with duration / 125 ms.

cut.use: A hard cut: the shape is simply there on the next frame (Bass's cut-on).

slideKey.use: Key positions for sliding bars before they are stepped: fast start, long ease-out.

anticipate.use: A small wind-up before a jump; sample on twos.

exit.use: Leaving: accelerate away in 2-3 drawings or simply cut.

cut-on.use: A shape or word appears on one frame. The default way things arrive.

pop.use: Emblem scales in from 0 via one overshoot drawing.

bar-wipe.use: Bass-style bars slide across the frame to reveal type or the emblem; 3-5 bars, staggered 83 ms.

slide.use: A shape moves to its next position in 4 drawings.

morph.use: One shape becomes the next idea (a starburst into a flower, a kidney into a fish) in 6 drawings.

hop.use: Character beat: anticipation, jump, landing squash.

blink.use: Eyes close for one drawing on threes.

boil.use: Optional: 3 slightly different drawings of a line cycled on threes, the hand-drawn 'boil'. Only on one element, only on screens over 400 px.

hold.use: Stillness between moves; the poster must be readable during every hold.

durations.$comment: Durations are whole numbers of drawings. Round any duration to the nearest multiple of 83 ms (twos) or 125 ms (threes).
durations.formula: drawings = 3 + 1 per 15% of the artboard travelled (max 8); duration = drawings x 83 ms on twos

order: bars wipe or field shape cuts on
headline cuts on or is revealed by a bar
choreography.sequential: Moves do not overlap: one thing moves, then holds, then the next moves. This is the opposite of smooth overlapping choreography.

titleSequence.use: Video intros, launch reels, hero animations.
titleSequence.pattern: Abstract shapes move to music, assemble into the emblem, title appears with the final hold.
titleSequence.source: Bass, The Man with the Golden Arm (1955): moving bars resolve into the arm (research.md 2.1).

loop.endsOn: A held frame that works as a poster on its own, held for at least 500 ms.

rules: Hold, then snap: every move is followed by a hold of at least 500 ms.
Step all motion on twos or threes; only snaps of 2-4 frames run on ones.
Shapes cut on, pop, slide as bars or morph. Never fade the artwork in.
One thing moves at a time; no overlapping moves.
No camera moves, parallax, 3D rotation or motion blur.
Type cuts on or is revealed by a bar; type never bounces or morphs.
With reduced motion: show the final held frame; no boil, no loops.
